s0001.literal: In the third year, spring, first month, on guihai day, the restoration of the Temple of the Sage was completed.
s0001.idiomatic: In the third year, on guihai day of the first month of spring, work on the Temple of the Sage was finished.

s0002.literal: On gengwu day, the mutual market with Goryeo was abolished.
s0002.idiomatic: On gengwu day the border market with Goryeo was closed.

s0003.literal: Prince Tachar requested the establishment of iron smelting works; this was granted.
s0003.idiomatic: Prince Tachar asked to set up iron smelting works, and the request was granted.

s0004.literal: He requested the establishment of a mutual market; this was not granted.
s0004.idiomatic: He also asked to open a border market, but that was refused.

s0005.literal: The people under Qulqul suffered famine; tribute sheep were abolished.
s0005.idiomatic: The people under Prince Qulqul were starving, so the court stopped collecting tribute sheep from them.

s0006.literal: Seven hundred silver-smelting households and one hundred forty Henan garrison-farming households were ordered to pay taxes and levies to their prefectures and counties.
s0006.idiomatic: Seven hundred silver-smelting households and one hundred forty Henan garrison-farming households were ordered to pay taxes through their local prefectures and counties.

s0007.literal: Artisan households serving as soldiers were ordered to remain soldiers; their military officers were to assess rich and poor ranks and provide relief to those without means.
s0007.idiomatic: Artisan households already serving as soldiers were to remain in service. Their officers were to rank households by wealth and poverty and give relief to those who could not support themselves.

s0008.literal: Yelü Zhuo went to Beijing to supply the princes' armies, and Pacification Commissioner Chai Zhen and others were also dispatched to purchase at increased price thirty thousand shi of rice to supplement them.
s0008.idiomatic: Yelü Zhuo went to Beijing to provision the princes' armies, and Pacification Commissioner Chai Zhen and others were sent to buy thirty thousand shi of rice at premium prices as additional supplies.

s0009.literal: The calendar was granted to the state of Goryeo.
s0009.idiomatic: The court granted Goryeo the official calendar.

s0010.literal: On xinwei day, garrison soldiers on all circuits and powerful families were forbidden to graze livestock so as to damage mulberry, jujube, and grain crops.
s0010.idiomatic: On xinwei day an edict forbade garrison troops on every circuit and powerful households from grazing livestock in fields of mulberry, jujube, and grain.

s0011.literal: On guiyou day, because the people had been worn down by military mobilization, an edict ordered that public and private arrears cease to be collected.
s0011.idiomatic: On guiyou day, citing the people's exhaustion from war mobilization, the Emperor ordered a halt to collecting public and private debts.

s0012.literal: On guiwei day, Prince Guangning Jadu was granted a camel-button gold-plated silver seal, and Prince Qebek a field-campaign seal.
s0012.idiomatic: On guiwei day Prince Guangning Jadu received a camel-button gold-plated silver seal, and Prince Qebek a seal for field command.

s0013.literal: Song Commissioner Jia Sidao sent letters to entice Commanders Zhang Yuan and others; Li Tan captured the letters and submitted them.
s0013.idiomatic: Jia Sidao, the Song commissioner, wrote letters trying to win over Commanders Zhang Yuan and others. Li Tan seized the letters and forwarded them to court.

s0014.literal: On bingxu day, Great Governor of Jiang-Han Shi Quan and Bozhou Wanhu Zhang Hongyan were ordered to lead eight thousand troops to Yan.
s0014.idiomatic: On bingxu day Shi Quan, Great Governor of Jiang-Han, and Zhang Hongyan, wanhu of Bozhou, were ordered to march eight thousand men to Yan.

s0015.literal: Palace suspended bells and chimes, music and dance, reed pipes and feathered dancers were prepared — three hundred sixty-two persons in all.
s0015.idiomatic: The court prepared palace bells and chimes, dancers, reed pipes, and feathered performers — three hundred sixty-two people in all.

s0016.literal: Goryeo dispatched envoys bearing a memorial to express thanks; a gracious edict replied to them.
s0016.idiomatic: Goryeo sent envoys with a memorial of thanks, and the Emperor answered with a gracious edict.

s0017.literal: Li Tan's hostage son Yan Jian escaped and returned home.
s0017.idiomatic: Yan Jian, Li Tan's son held at court as a hostage, fled home.

s0018.literal: Second month, dinghai new moon: those originally registered as soldiers who had falsely registered as civilians were ordered restored to their proper status by the relevant offices.
s0018.idiomatic: On the dinghai new moon of the second month, men originally on the military rolls who had hidden themselves among civilians were ordered back onto the registers.

s0019.literal: Deserters from all circuits were conscripted.
s0019.idiomatic: The court conscripted deserters from every circuit.

s0020.literal: On jichou day, Li Tan rebelled, ceded the three cities of Lian and Hai to the Song, killed all the Mongol garrison troops, and led his followers toward Yidu.
s0020.idiomatic: On jichou day Li Tan rose in rebellion. He handed three cities in the Lian and Hai region to the Song, slaughtered every Mongol garrison soldier there, and marched his forces toward Yidu.

s0021.literal: Former Deputy Pacification Commissioner Wang Pan escaped to Jinan. Summoned by courier, he was questioned for counsel by Yao Shu; Wang replied: "The foolish boy is arrogant — he will soon be captured."
s0021.idiomatic: Wang Pan, former deputy pacification commissioner, had slipped away to Jinan. The Emperor summoned him by courier and had Yao Shu ask his counsel. Wang answered, "That arrogant fool will be taken in no time."

s0023.literal: On gengyin day, Song troops attacked Xincai.
s0023.idiomatic: On gengyin day Song forces attacked Xincai.

s0024.literal: On xinmao day, official salaries at court and in the provinces were first fixed, and Grand Minister of Agriculture Yao Shu was ordered to compile the regulations.
s0024.idiomatic: On xinmao day the court first fixed official salaries at court and in the provinces and ordered Yao Shu, Grand Minister of Agriculture, to draft the regulations.

s0025.literal: On jiawu day, Li Tan entered Yidu and opened the treasury to reward his officers.
s0025.idiomatic: On jiawu day Li Tan entered Yidu, opened the government stores, and rewarded his commanders.

s0026.literal: On yiwei day, an edict ordered all circuits to use this year's civilian levies to purchase horses.
s0026.idiomatic: On yiwei day an edict ordered every circuit to use the year's civilian tax receipts to buy horses.

s0027.literal: On bingshen day, Guo Shoujing completed the Baoshan water clock, and it was moved to Yanjing.
s0027.idiomatic: On bingshen day Guo Shoujing finished the Baoshan clepsydra, which was then moved to Yanjing.

s0028.literal: Xing, Song, and Yun Prefectures were placed under the jurisdiction of Shangdu.
s0028.idiomatic: Xing, Song, and Yun Prefectures were placed under Shangdu.

s0029.literal: On xinchou day, Li Tan sent cavalry to raid Putai.
s0029.idiomatic: On xinchou day Li Tan sent horsemen to raid Putai.

s0030.literal: On guimao day, an edict ordered troops dispatched to suppress him.
s0030.idiomatic: On guimao day an edict ordered armies sent to crush the rebellion.

s0031.literal: Zhao Bi was made Grand Councillor.
s0031.idiomatic: Zhao Bi was appointed grand councillor.

s0032.literal: The four cities of Shen, Ji, Nangong, and Zaoqiang were repaired.
s0032.idiomatic: Fortifications at Shen, Ji, Nangong, and Zaoqiang were repaired.

s0033.literal: On jiachen day, Mongol and Han armies were dispatched to suppress Li Tan. Naval Wanhu Jie Cheng and Zhang Rongshi, Daming Wanhu Wang Wengan, and Wanhu Yan Zhongfan were ordered to assemble at Dongping; Jinan Wanhu Zhang Hong, Guide Wanhu Di Jia, and Wuwei Army catapult marshal Xue Junsheng and others were ordered to assemble at Bin-Di. An edict ordered Jinan Circuit Military-Civilian Wanhu Zhang Hong and Bin-Di Circuit Pacification Commissioner Han Shi'an each to repair walls and moats and mobilize all people within their jurisdictions as soldiers for defense.
s0033.idiomatic: On jiachen day Mongol and Han forces marched against Li Tan. The naval commanders Jie Cheng and Zhang Rongshi, Daming wanhu Wang Wengan, and wanhu Yan Zhongfan were to gather at Dongping; Jinan wanhu Zhang Hong, Guide wanhu Di Jia, and Wuwei Army catapult marshal Xue Junsheng and others were to gather in Bin-Di. Zhang Hong, military-civilian wanhu of Jinan, and Han Shi'an, pacification commissioner of Bin-Di, were each ordered to repair walls and ditches and draft every man under their jurisdiction for defense.

s0034.literal: Zhang Rou and his son Zhang Hongfan were summoned to lead two thousand troops to the capital.
s0034.idiomatic: Zhang Rou and his son Zhang Hongfan were called to the capital with two thousand troops.

s0035.literal: On bingwu day, Prince Qebek was ordered to command all armies overall; Bojinai and Zhao Bi were to administer branch secretariat affairs in Shandong, Song Zizhen to serve as counsellor of branch secretariat affairs, and Dong Yuan and Gao Yimin as left and right bureau directors, granted discretionary authority.
s0035.idiomatic: On bingwu day Prince Qebek was placed in overall command of the armies. Bojinai and Zhao Bi were to run the branch secretariat in Shandong, Song Zizhen as its counsellor, and Dong Yuan and Gao Yimin as left and right bureau directors with authority to act as circumstances required.

s0036.literal: Troops from the circuits of Zhending, Shuntian, Hejian, Pingluan, Daming, Xingzhou, and Henan all assembled at Jinan.
s0036.idiomatic: Forces from Zhending, Shuntian, Hejian, Pingluan, Daming, Xingzhou, and Henan all converged on Jinan.

s0037.literal: Left Associate of the Central Secretariat Kuoku, Minister Qieliemen, and Pacification Commissioner You Xian were sent to administer the Pacification Commission at Daming; the Luozi, Huaizhou, Zhangde, Weihui, and eastern and western Henan circuits were all placed under it.
s0037.idiomatic: Kuoku, left associate of the Central Secretariat, Qieliemen, minister of state, and Pacification Commissioner You Xian were sent to run the pacification commission at Daming, with the Luozi, Huaizhou, Zhangde, Weihui, and eastern and western Henan circuits placed under them.

s0038.literal: On jiyou day, Wang Wentong was executed for plotting with Li Tan, and an edict was issued to inform the realm within and without.
s0038.idiomatic: On jiyou day Wang Wentong was put to death for conspiring with Li Tan, and an edict announced the sentence throughout the empire.

s0039.literal: Wang Yan and others were executed for seditious speech.
s0039.idiomatic: Wang Yan and others were executed for spreading seditious talk.

s0040.literal: On xinhai day, an edict ordered Marshal Ahai to divide his troops to garrison Pingluan, Haikou, Dongjing, Guangning, and Yizhou, and bring the remaining troops to the capital.
s0040.idiomatic: On xinhai day Marshal Ahai was ordered to detach troops to garrison Pingluan, Haikou, Dongjing, Guangning, and Yizhou and to bring the rest of his force to the capital.

s0041.literal: An edict ordered all circuits to conscript deserters back into garrison farming, with strict enforcement of the prohibition.
s0041.idiomatic: An edict ordered every circuit to hunt down deserters and return them to garrison farming, with the ban strictly enforced.

s0042.literal: On renzi day, Li Tan seized Jinan.
s0042.idiomatic: On renzi day Li Tan took Jinan.

s0043.literal: On guichou day, an edict ordered the circuits of Daming, Luozi, Zhangde, Weihui, Huaizhou, Henan, Zhending, Xingzhou, Shuntian, Hejian, and Pingluan all to register troops and garrison the cities.
s0043.idiomatic: On guichou day an edict ordered Daming, Luozi, Zhangde, Weihui, Huaizhou, Henan, Zhending, Xingzhou, Shuntian, Hejian, and Pingluan to register soldiers and man their city walls.

s0045.literal: On bingchen day, an edict ordered Badu Motai to lead the Xizhou garrison troops to Jinan and move its people to Caizhou; Dongping Wanhu Yan Zhongfan was to leave troops to garrison Suzhou and Qixian and follow with the remainder.
s0045.idiomatic: On bingchen day Badu Motai was ordered to take the Xizhou garrison to Jinan and relocate its people to Caizhou. Yan Zhongfan, wanhu of Dongping, was to leave troops at Suzhou and Qixian and march with the rest.

s0046.literal: Third month, wuwu day, an imperial directive stated: "Documents not from the Central Secretariat, and reports to the Secretariat not submitted by military-civilian officials, are not permitted to enter the courier system."
s0046.idiomatic: On wuwu day of the third month the Emperor directed that only Central Secretariat documents and submissions from military-civilian officials to the Secretariat might enter the courier system.

s0047.literal: On jiwei day, household males of Muslims, Uighurs, Nestorian Christians, Dasman, and others were conscripted as soldiers.
s0047.idiomatic: On jiwei day males from Muslim, Uighur, Nestorian Christian, Dasman, and other registered households were drafted as soldiers.

s0048.literal: On gengshen day, household males of the Beijing falconry offices and related households were conscripted as soldiers, their levies were remitted, and Zhao Bing was ordered to command them.
s0048.idiomatic: On gengshen day males from the Beijing falconry offices and related households were drafted as soldiers, exempted from levies, and placed under Zhao Bing's command.

s0049.literal: On xinyou day, Zongbatu reported that in Henan there were men willing to enlist voluntarily; they were ordered immediately placed under command.
s0049.idiomatic: On xinyou day Zongbatu reported volunteers for military service in Henan, and they were ordered enlisted at once.

s0050.literal: Zheng Ding, Shams al-Din, Dalidai, and San-dao were dispatched to administer pacification affairs at Pingyang and Taiyuan.
s0050.idiomatic: Zheng Ding, Shams al-Din, Dalidai, and San-dao were sent to administer pacification at Pingyang and Taiyuan.

s0051.literal: Currently serving civilian officials, falconry households, artisan households, and others were drafted as soldiers.
s0051.idiomatic: Serving civilian officials together with falconry and artisan households were drafted into the army.

s0052.literal: Hongzhou brocade workers and embroiderers were moved to the capital.
s0052.idiomatic: Brocade workers and embroiderers from Hongzhou were relocated to the capital.

s0053.literal: An edict ordered the previously conscripted Jinzhou troops of the two Hedong circuits placed under Zheng Ding's command.
s0053.idiomatic: An edict placed the Jinzhou troops previously drafted from the two Hedong circuits under Zheng Ding's command.

s0054.literal: An edict appointed Grand Councillors Mamma and Lian Xixian, Vice Councillor Shang Ting, and Judicial Officer Maixiao to administer the branch secretariat in Shaanxi and Sichuan.
s0054.idiomatic: An edict sent Grand Councillors Mamma and Lian Xixian, Vice Councillor Shang Ting, and judicial officer Maixiao to run the branch secretariat in Shaanxi and Sichuan.

s0055.literal: More than forty private merchants caught at the southern frontier were ordered released.
s0055.idiomatic: More than forty private merchants seized at the southern border were ordered released.

s0056.literal: An edict ordered eight gyrfalcon courier stations established between Yanjing and Jinan.
s0056.idiomatic: An edict established eight gyrfalcon relay stations between Yanjing and Jinan.

s0057.literal: On renshen day, Households Minister Liu Su was assigned sole responsibility for paper currency law, with Grand Councillor Sayyid Ajall concurrently overseeing it.
s0057.idiomatic: On renshen day Liu Su, minister of households, was put in charge of paper currency regulations, with Grand Councillor Sayyid Ajall concurrently supervising the work.

s0058.literal: Sags and Chai Zhen were sent to administer pacification affairs at Beijing.
s0058.idiomatic: Sags and Chai Zhen were dispatched to run pacification affairs at Beijing.

s0059.literal: This year's silk and silver levies were remitted; only land rent was to be paid.
s0059.idiomatic: Silk and silver levies for the year were waived; only land rent was collected.

s0060.literal: On guiyou day, Shi Shu and Aju were each ordered to lead troops to Jinan.
s0060.idiomatic: On guiyou day Shi Shu and Aju were each ordered to march on Jinan.

s0061.literal: They encountered Li Tan's army, intercepted and routed it, beheaded four thousand, and Tan retreated to hold Jinan.
s0061.idiomatic: They met Li Tan's army, cut them off, and routed them, taking four thousand heads. Li Tan fell back to defend Jinan.

s0062.literal: On yihai day, Song General Xia Gui attacked Fuli.
s0062.idiomatic: On yihai day the Song general Xia Gui attacked Fuli.

s0063.literal: On wuyin day, Wanhu Han Shi'an, leading Pacification Commissioner Ma Xing and Qianhu Zhang Jimin, routed Li Tan's army at Gaoyuan, captured his provisional governor Fu Gui, and granted Zhang Jimin and Ma Xing gold tally tokens.
s0063.idiomatic: On wuyin day Han Shi'an, wanhu, with Pacification Commissioner Ma Xing and qianhu Zhang Jimin, crushed Li Tan's force at Gaoyuan, captured his acting prefect Fu Gui, and awarded Zhang Jimin and Ma Xing gold tally tokens.

s0064.literal: An edict announced Li Tan's defeat to all circuits.
s0064.idiomatic: An edict reported Li Tan's defeat to every circuit.

s0065.literal: Private possession of military weapons by the people was forbidden.
s0065.idiomatic: The people were forbidden to keep military weapons in private hands.

s0066.literal: On renwu day, Uighur script was first used for courier imperial seals and documents.
s0066.idiomatic: On renwu day Uighur script was first used on imperial seals and documents sent by courier.

s0067.literal: Xijing's silk and silver taxes for this year were remitted.
s0067.idiomatic: Silk and silver taxes at Xijing were waived for the year.

s0068.literal: On jiashen day, Goryeo liquor taxes were remitted.
s0068.idiomatic: On jiashen day Goryeo's liquor tax was waived.

s0069.literal: On yiyou day, Song Xia Gui attacked Qixian.
s0069.idiomatic: On yiyou day Xia Gui of the Song attacked Qixian.

s0070.literal: Officials governing the people on all circuits were instructed not to allow armies, envoys, and others to enter prefectural cities, villages, or market towns and disturb peaceful civilians.
s0070.idiomatic: Officials on every circuit were told not to let armies, envoys, or other parties enter prefectural cities, villages, or market towns and harass the people.

s0071.literal: Fourth month of summer, bingwu new moon: the great army erected palisades and dug trenches, besieging Tan at Jinan.
s0071.idiomatic: On the bingwu new moon of the fourth month of summer the main army threw up palisades and trenches and besieged Li Tan in Jinan.

s0072.literal: On dinghai day, an edict ordered that military and civilian personnel in Boxing, Gaoyuan, and other places who had once been coerced into following Li Tan were all pardoned.
s0072.idiomatic: On dinghai day an edict pardoned soldiers and civilians in Boxing, Gaoyuan, and elsewhere who had been forced to follow Li Tan.

s0073.literal: On gengyin day, Qieliemen and Pacification Commissioner Zhang Geng were ordered to divide Xingzhou households between two darughachi.
s0073.idiomatic: On gengyin day Qieliemen and Pacification Commissioner Zhang Geng were ordered to split Xingzhou households between two darughachi.

s0074.literal: On xinmao day, the Yu Temple at Hezhong was restored and granted the name Jianji Palace.
s0074.idiomatic: On xinmao day the Yu Temple at Hezhong was restored and renamed Jianji Palace.

s0075.literal: On renchen day, Pu Yuangui, commander of military and civilian affairs of the Daliang-Luzhou Circuit, was made Military Commissioner of the Eastern Kui Circuit.
s0075.idiomatic: On renchen day Pu Yuangui, commander of military and civilian affairs of the Daliang-Luzhou circuit, was appointed military commissioner of the Eastern Kui circuit.

s0076.literal: On bingshen day, Song commanders Hua Lufen and Grand Marshal Tang attacked Xu and Pi Prefectures.
s0076.idiomatic: On bingshen day the Song commanders Hua Lufen and Grand Marshal Tang attacked Xu and Pi Prefectures.

s0077.literal: An edict ordered one thousand of Zhang Rou's troops returned to garrison Bozhou.
s0077.idiomatic: An edict sent one thousand of Zhang Rou's men back to garrison Bozhou.

s0078.literal: On gengzi day, Jiang-Han Great Governor Shi Quan executed Zhao Baihu and his followers for deserting and returning.
s0078.idiomatic: On gengzi day Shi Quan, Great Governor of Jiang-Han, executed Zhao Baihu and his men for desertion.

s0079.literal: An edict stated: "From now on, when retainers commit serious crimes and interrogation establishes the facts, a report must first be submitted to the throne before legal punishment is applied."
s0079.idiomatic: An edict declared, "Henceforth, when retainers commit capital offenses and inquiry proves the charge, the case must first be reported to the throne before sentence is carried out."

s0080.literal: An edict ordered the people of Xu and Pi settled, forbidding garrison troops and powerful officials from grazing livestock so as to damage their grain crops, mulberry, and jujube.
s0080.idiomatic: Another edict ordered the people of Xu and Pi resettled and forbade garrison soldiers and powerful officials from grazing livestock over their grain, mulberry, and jujube.

s0081.literal: One thousand shi of rice and three hundred oxen were given to Mongol households at Xijing.
s0081.idiomatic: The court gave one thousand shi of rice and three hundred oxen to Mongol households at Xijing.

s0082.literal: On guimao day, Song troops attacked Bozhou.
s0082.idiomatic: On guimao day Song forces attacked Bozhou.

s0083.literal: On jiachen day, the branch secretariat, pacification commissions, darughachi on all circuits, and officials governing the people were ordered to encourage the people to open and cultivate land, plant mulberry and jujube, and not to undertake unauthorized non-urgent corvée that would interfere with the farming season.
s0083.idiomatic: On jiachen day the branch secretariat, pacification commissions, circuit darughachi, and civilian officials were ordered to encourage farming, mulberry planting, and jujube cultivation, and not to impose unauthorized non-urgent labor that would steal time from the fields.

s0084.literal: On yisi day, because Beijing, Guangning, Hao, and Yizhou had been worn down by military mobilization, this year's taxes and levies were remitted.
s0084.idiomatic: On yisi day Beijing, Guangning, Hao, and Yizhou were exempted from the year's taxes and levies because war mobilization had exhausted them.

s0085.literal: Officials on all circuits were ordered to review wrongful convictions carefully.
s0085.idiomatic: Every circuit was ordered to review cases of wrongful conviction with care.

s0086.literal: An edict ordered the two Hedong circuits together with the darughachi and military-civilian officials of Pingyang and Taiyuan to pacify soldiers and civilians, each maintaining livelihood without missing the year's quotas.
s0086.idiomatic: An edict told the two Hedong circuits and the darughachi and military-civilian officials of Pingyang and Taiyuan to settle troops and people in their occupations without missing the year's revenue targets.

s0087.literal: On dingwei day, Li Tan sent Chai Niuer to summon the local man Lu Guang; Guang bound and presented him, then killed him.
s0087.idiomatic: On dingwei day Li Tan sent Chai Niuer to win over the local man Lu Guang. Guang seized Niuer, handed him over, and had him executed.

s0088.literal: Guang was made Acting Military Judge of Weizhou and concurrently bandit-catcher.
s0088.idiomatic: Lu Guang was appointed acting military judge of Weizhou and bandit-catcher as well.

s0089.literal: On wushen day, Prince Yeshangge was granted a gold seal.
s0089.idiomatic: On wushen day Prince Yeshangge received a gold seal.

s0090.literal: On gengxu day, Prince Qebek was granted two gold and silver gyrfalcon tokens each.
s0090.idiomatic: On gengxu day Prince Qebek received two gold and two silver gyrfalcon courier tokens.

s0091.literal: New and old levies at Songzhou, Xingzhou, and Wangyunzhou were remitted; the revenues of Wangyun, Songshan, and Xingzhou were placed under Kaiping Prefecture.
s0091.idiomatic: Old and new levies at Songzhou, Xingzhou, and Wangyunzhou were waived, and revenues from Wangyun, Songshan, and Xingzhou were assigned to Kaiping Prefecture.

s0092.literal: On renzi day, an edict ordered that unless there was a military emergency, the Wangyun courier station was not to be used.
s0092.idiomatic: On renzi day an edict forbade use of the Wangyun relay station except in military emergencies.

s0093.literal: On yimao day, Wang Huozi, Zhang Wuseng, Du Xin, and others of Henan Circuit plotted sedition and were all executed.
s0093.idiomatic: On yimao day Wang Huozi, Zhang Wuseng, Du Xin, and others in Henan Circuit were executed for plotting rebellion.

s0094.literal: An edict ordered Right Grand Councillor Shi Tianze to command the campaign exclusively; all generals were to accept his orders.
s0094.idiomatic: An edict put Right Grand Councillor Shi Tianze in sole field command, with every general under his authority.

s0095.literal: Fifth month, wuwu day: Qixian fell; Acting Wanhu Li Yi and Qianhu Zhang Haogu died in its defense.
s0095.idiomatic: On wuwu day of the fifth month Qixian fell. Acting wanhu Li Yi and qianhu Zhang Haogu died defending it.

s0096.literal: On gengshen day, an encircling wall was built around Jinan; Tan could no longer get out.
s0096.idiomatic: On gengshen day a ring wall was thrown up around Jinan, and Li Tan was trapped inside.

s0097.literal: An edict ordered Sags to pacify the people of Yidu Circuit, each devoting themselves to farming, while forbidding Mongol and Han troops from plundering.
s0097.idiomatic: An edict sent Sags to settle the people of Yidu Circuit and keep them at their farming, while forbidding Mongol and Han soldiers from looting.

s0098.literal: On guihai day, Shi Quan falsely reported that Xu-Pi Commander Li Gaoge had recovered Pizhou; an edict pardoned Li Gaoge and those below him.
s0098.idiomatic: On guihai day Shi Quan falsely reported that Li Gaoge, commander of Xu and Pi, had retaken Pizhou. An edict pardoned Li Gaoge and his subordinates.

s0099.literal: At that time Song General Xia Gui was attacking Pizhou; Gaoge surrendered. After Gui departed, Gaoge declared that he had been able to preserve the prefectural city; Shi Quan reported this, hence the order.
s0099.idiomatic: At the time the Song general Xia Gui was attacking Pizhou and Li Gaoge surrendered. After Xia Gui withdrew, Li Gaoge claimed he had kept the city intact. Shi Quan reported this, which led to the pardon.

s0100.literal: On jiazi day, Song troops attacked Lijin County.
s0100.idiomatic: On jiazi day Song forces attacked Lijin County.
